question: What casing and orientation rules generally apply to word messages on signs?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In general, word messages on signs must be aligned horizontally and read left to right, and must use the standard wording shown in the MUTCD and the "Standard Highway Signs" publication. Casing rules vary by sign type: on community wayfinding guide signs (as on guide signs generally), destination names must use lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters, while all other word messages must be in all upper-case letters. Minor modifications to word message layout are allowed, but shapes and colors must remain as standardized. Standards (mandatory): - "Except as otherwise provided in this Manual, all word messages shall be aligned horizontally across a sign, reading left to right." - "Except as provided in Section 2A.04, all word messages shall use standard wording as shown in this Manual and in the 'Standard Highway Signs' publication (see Section 1A.05)." - "The lettering for destinations on community wayfinding guide signs shall be a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters (see Section 2D.04). All other word messages on community wayfinding guide signs shall be in all upper-case letters." - "Standardization of these designs does not preclude further improvement by minor modifications to the orientation of symbols (see Section 2A.09), width of borders, or layout of word messages, but all shapes and colors shall be as indicated." Guidance (recommended): - "Word messages should be as brief as practical and the lettering should be large enough to provide the necessary legibility distance." - For pavement marking word messages (a related orientation rule): "If a pavement marking word message consists of more than one line of information, it should read in the direction of travel. The first word of the message should be nearest to the road user." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 2L-3 shows CMS message examples displayed in all upper-case lettering, with a note that single-color CMS with pixel spacing greater than 20 mm use all upper-case lettering, while multi-color full-matrix CMS with pixel spacing of 20 mm or less should use upper- and lower-case lettering where appropriate. [Image 2] Figure 9D-5 accompanies shared-use path provisions requiring destination lettering to combine lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters, with all other word messages in all upper-case letters — paralleling the community wayfinding casing rule. Citations: - Section 2A.08 Standard §1 (p.45) - Section 2A.08 Standard §2 (p.45) - Section 2D.55 Standard §32 (p.271) - Section 2A.04 Standard §8 (p.40) - Section 2D.55 Guidance §28 (p.271) - Section 3B.21 Guidance §2 (p.575) - Table 2L-3 (p.517) - Figure 9D-5 (p.1082)
gold_answer: Word messages generally read horizontally from left to right. Place, street, and highway names use initial upper-case letters with lower-case letters; other legends use upper-case letters unless another MUTCD provision specifies otherwise.
